[2003/Toyota/RAV4] Trying to determine what this noise is from
This noise is pretty constant in my car and I can't exactly tell what the deal is. I've asked around and so far gotten all kinds of answers that haven't helped me actually determine what's going on.
How easy is it to rock the engine with your hand? Could be a lot of issues, but almost sounds like an engine mount.

Heya Ash!

First, before we get into any specifics, check your oil level. I've had random noises come up from engines with a low oil level that go away when filled correctly. The empty space serves as a harmonic chamber that resonates engine sounds.

Second, which noise are you talking about? In the video I hear a higher-pitched, fast-paced, constant tapping sound, and a lower-pitched, slower, rhythmic sound. It sounds like you're focusing on the lower-pitched slower rhythmic sound, but I can't be certain.

The tapping is most certainly your lifters. They're generally pretty audible on 1AZ-FE 2.0 Toyota engines. They're also a pain to adjust and not generally needed unless you have major engine work done.

The lower-pitched rhythmic noise sounds more like something being driven by the accessory drive, or it could be something failing internally in the block. If you're mechanically inclined at all, try taking the accessory belt off and turning the engine on for long enough to see if the noise goes away. That will tell you whether you're dealing with a failing water pump/alternator/pulley or if it's internal to the engine.
